  Terse gloss: "Ananias — name borne by three NT figures: the deceitful husband, the Damascus disciple, and the high priest"
  Readable gloss: "Ἀνανίας (Ananias), the Greek form of Hebrew Hananiah ('the LORD is gracious'), identifies three distinct persons in Acts. First, Ananias the husband of Sapphira, who lied about the sale price of property and fell dead at Peter's feet (Acts 5:1-5). Second, Ananias the devout disciple in Damascus whom the Lord sent to restore Saul's sight and baptize him (Acts 9:10-17; 22:12). Third, Ananias the high priest who presided over Paul's trial before the Sanhedrin and whom Paul sharply rebuked as a 'whitewashed wall' (Acts 23:2; 24:1). Spanish 'Ananías' preserves the name across all three referents."

This episode became a sobering paradigm of divine judgment on dishonesty within the covenant community.
